title: Dear Helen, I'm Bored

pre.en: Why does Helen thank Matt at the end?
pre.zh: 最后 Helen 为什么要谢谢 Matt？
options: He used to play football with her brother.
He gave her some good advice.
He promised to take up pottery.
He was her only caller that night.

intro: 这是一档电台热线节目：在保险公司上班的 Matt 打进电话，说自己每天晚上都很无聊，主持人 Helen 给他出主意。Helen 讲起自己小时候在乡下的日子，用的是 would + 动词原形：回忆过去经常、反复做的事。留意它和 Matt 说的 used to 有什么不同。结尾有个小反转。

sentences.en: You're listening to Dear Helen, and our first caller is Matt from Bristol.
sentences.zh: 这里是《亲爱的 Helen》，第一位打进电话的是布里斯托尔的 Matt。
sentences.speaker: Helen

sentences.en: Hi, Matt, what's on your mind?
sentences.zh: 你好，Matt，有什么烦心事？

sentences.en: Hi, Helen.
sentences.zh: 你好，Helen。
sentences.speaker: Matt

sentences.en: Well, I'm thirty-four, and I work in an insurance office.
sentences.zh: 是这样，我今年三十四，在一家保险公司上班。

sentences.en: Every evening I get home at six, grab a bite and sit on the same sofa with the same three apps until midnight.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上六点到家，随便吃两口，然后坐在同一张沙发上，刷同样三个 App，一直刷到半夜。

sentences.en: I used to play five-a-side football on Thursdays, but the team broke up.
sentences.zh: 我以前每周四踢五人制足球，后来球队散了。

sentences.en: Now my boots just live in a drawer.
sentences.zh: 现在我的球鞋就一直躺在抽屉里。

sentences.en: Even when I'm out of the office on holiday, I just kill time on my phone.
sentences.zh: 就连休假不用上班的时候，我也就是拿着手机打发时间。

sentences.en: First of all, there's nothing wrong with you, and you're not lazy.
sentences.zh: 首先，你没什么毛病，也不懒。
sentences.speaker: Helen

sentences.en: You're stuck in a rut, and that's a different thing.
sentences.zh: 你只是陷进一成不变的日子里了，这是两码事。

sentences.en: No wonder the evenings feel long — they're all the same evening.
sentences.zh: 难怪晚上显得那么长——每个晚上都是同一个晚上。

sentences.en: Ha.
sentences.zh: 哈。
sentences.speaker: Matt

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly how it feels.
sentences.zh: 对，就是这种感觉。

sentences.en: Believe me, I know all about boredom.
sentences.zh: 相信我，无聊是什么滋味，我太清楚了。
sentences.speaker: Helen

sentences.en: I grew up in a village in Somerset with one bus a day.
sentences.zh: 我在萨默塞特的一个村子里长大，那儿一天就一趟公交车。

sentences.en: In the summer holidays, I would lie on the kitchen floor for hours, staring at the ceiling.
sentences.zh: 放暑假的时候，我常常在厨房地板上一躺就是好几个小时，盯着天花板发呆。

sentences.en: My brother and I would make up games, and the rules changed every five minutes.
sentences.zh: 我和我哥会自己编游戏，规则五分钟一变。

sentences.en: We'd walk to the bus stop just to see who got off.
sentences.zh: 我们还会走到车站，就为了看看谁下车。

sentences.en: And I'd write terrible poems about the farmer's goat.
sentences.zh: 我还会给农场主家的山羊写特别烂的诗。

sentences.en: Actually, my whole career dates back to those poems.
sentences.zh: 说起来，我这一行能干到今天，就是从那些诗开始的。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的假的？
sentences.speaker: Matt

sentences.en: Really.
sentences.zh: 真的。
sentences.speaker: Helen

sentences.en: Here's my advice.
sentences.zh: 我给你几条建议。

sentences.en: First, get out of the house twice a week, even if it's only to the library.
sentences.zh: 第一，每周出门两次，哪怕只是去趟图书馆。

sentences.en: Second, take up something you'll probably be bad at.
sentences.zh: 第二，学一样你多半学不好的东西。

sentences.en: Pottery and salsa are both on the menu at your local college.
sentences.zh: 你们那儿的成人学院就开着陶艺课和萨尔萨舞课。

sentences.en: Leave your phone at home, or you'll only get distracted.
sentences.zh: 手机放家里，不然你只会分心。

sentences.en: Ring back in three months and tell me what changes you've made to your evenings.
sentences.zh: 三个月后再打进来，告诉我你的晚上有了哪些变化。

sentences.en: Calling tonight was a good first step, so keep up the good work.
sentences.zh: 今晚打这个电话就是很好的第一步，继续保持。

sentences.en: Thanks, Helen.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，Helen。
sentences.speaker: Matt

sentences.en: I will.
sentences.zh: 我会的。

sentences.en: And Matt?
sentences.zh: 还有，Matt？
sentences.speaker: Helen

sentences.en: To be honest, you're my only caller tonight.
sentences.zh: 说实话，今晚就你一个人打进来。

sentences.en: I've had a lot of time on my hands, so thanks.
sentences.zh: 我闲了一晚上，所以真得谢谢你。

sentences.en: You've made my evening.
sentences.zh: 你让我这一晚上都值了。

cards.note: 电台、电视的热线节目里打电话进来的人；打进节目说 call in / ring in。
买保险是 take out insurance；重音在第二个音节 in-SUR-ance。
to eat something quickly

cards.zh: 不在办公室；外出（不上班）
cards.note: to be away from work, for example on holiday or at an appointment
to do something unimportant while you are waiting or have nothing to do
cards.tip: 常带「没什么意义」的意思；花时间做正经事用 spend time doing。
cards.example: We killed time in a café until the train came.

cards.zh: 陷入一成不变的日子；困在老套路里
cards.note: to be in a boring situation where you do the same things every day and nothing changes
cards.tip: rut 原指车轮压出来的沟，车陷进去就出不来；也说 get stuck in a rut。
cards.example: After ten years in the same job, she felt stuck in a rut.

cards.note: used to say that something is not surprising
cards.tip: 后面直接接句子；单独说也行：No wonder!（怪不得！）
cards.example: You didn't eat lunch? No wonder you're hungry.

cards.note: bored（人觉得无聊）的名词；boring 是「事情让人无聊」。
读 /ˈsiːlɪŋ/，c 发 s 的音。
绵羊是 sheep，单复数同形。
to have existed since a particular time in the past
cards.tip: 不用进行时，也不用被动：不说 is dated back to。
cards.example: The church dates back to the twelfth century.

cards.zh: 出门走走；别老待在家里
cards.note: to go out, especially when you have been at home for too long
cards.tip: 重点不是去哪儿，而是「离开家」；比 go out 更强调在家闷太久了。
cards.example: I work from home, so I go to the gym just to get out of the house.

cards.note: to start doing a new activity, especially for fun
cards.tip: 后面接名词或 doing：take up yoga、take up painting；不接 to do。
cards.example: My dad took up running when he was sixty.

cards.note: 做陶艺的课叫 a pottery class。
拉丁舞的一种；也是一种番茄辣酱。
available to eat at a meal or in a restaurant
cards.tip: 这里是比喻：课程表上有这些课可选。
cards.example: Fish and chips is always on the menu on Fridays.

cards.note: to stop paying attention to what you are doing because something else gets your interest
to change parts of something
cards.tip: 动词用 make，不用 do；对什么做改动用 to。
cards.example: We made a few changes to the plan after the meeting.

cards.note: used to tell someone to continue doing something well
used before you say what you really think, especially something the listener may not like

cards.zh: 闲着没事；有大把空闲时间
cards.note: to have a lot of free time and not much to do
cards.tip: your 要跟着主语换：I have time on my hands / she has time on her hands。
cards.example: Now that the kids have left home, I have more time on my hands.
